text:
Alex Tuch's biggest story this month wasn't a goal. In The Players' Tribune he thanked the nurses at Sisters Hospital in Buffalo for saving his newborn son's life, an essay that reached well beyond hockey. On the ice, in his first season in Washington after 360 games as a Sabre, he leads the Capitals with 12 goals in 19 games.

The goals come with a footnote: 12 on 8.7 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 25% against 17% last season, and that rate rarely lasts. But the chances themselves are real and up sharply from last year, and the Capitals take 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice. The odd part is the assists: only two all season, none in his last 10 games, even though Washington has scored 5.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. That usually swings back.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a strong setup man last season, so the passing should show up. Watch for the assists to arrive as the shooting cools.
